header.stance: 回購支撐長債，Fed通膨疑慮未解

zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 長期借款成本攀升，財政部出手加碼回購

美國財政部長貝森特週三宣布，將用於支持市場流動性的10至30年期公債回購規模至少加倍，帶動長債買盤回流。財政部才在兩週前的季度融資公告中維持原計畫不變，這次意外調整使30年期殖利率下跌9個基點至5.19%，10年期下跌6個基點至4.65%，2年期則持平於4.19%。

10年期殖利率的降幅全數來自實質殖利率，損益兩平通膨率仍為2.30%，並未顯示市場下修通膨預期。長債殖利率先前升破5.30%後，財政部承諾吸收更多供給，美元隨之跌至3個月低點，黃金大漲。同日公布的Fed七月會議紀錄卻顯示，支持升息的官員仍不少。債務管理措施緩解了長端壓力，央行的通膨疑慮並未因此消失。

企業仍持續籌措大筆資金。Alphabet首度發行澳幣債，規模高於原先規劃，訂單充足，但最長天期仍付出6.98%的殖利率。Nebius再次發行可轉債；以Anthropic為主要租戶的德州開發案，則在Google保證的優先債務之下引入夾層融資。AI資金需求正擴及更多幣別與資本結構。公債殖利率下降有助降低成本，但誰提供保證、誰承擔施工或股權風險，仍直接左右融資條件。

## 回購改變供給結構，無法消除財政赤字

擴大回購將於9月9日開始。財政部原先公布、涵蓋至11月4日的暫定時程，安排最多$140億買進10至30年期公債；規模加倍意味至少再增加$140億。Barclays估計，每季額外買進金額約$160億，相當於20年期與30年期全年發行量的15%。相對整體美債市場，金額並不算大，但足以影響民間投資人需要承接的長期債券供給。

宣布時點強化了市場反應。財政部通常在季度再融資公告中調整回購參數，兩週前才確認原有安排，如今卻在季中改動。即使交易秩序正常，這仍透露長期借款成本已升至官員難以忽視的水準。投資人除了估算既定供給，也得考慮殖利率再升時，財政部是否會進一步介入。

當日交易相當活躍。按原始面額計算，美債成交金額達$1.370兆，較前一交易日增加28.1%；其中一般附息公債為$1.112兆，增加31.5%。7至10年期成交額增加53.1%至$2,343億，20年以上增加52.0%至$1,707億，交易商與客戶之間的交易占比分別為39.9%與46.0%。這些數字是成交額，不是淨流入，但足以看出漲勢並非發生在交投清淡的市場。20年以上政府債券指數上漲1.69%，1至3年期僅上漲0.03%。

5年期殖利率收低2個基點至4.35%。長端降幅更大，使2年與10年期利差縮小6個基點至46個基點，2年與30年期縮小9個基點至100個基點。10年期實質殖利率降至2.35%；30年期名目與實質殖利率同樣下跌9個基點。不過，10年與30年期名目殖利率仍分別高於1個月前10與13個基點，10年期損益兩平通膨率也高出6個基點。

財政部尚未說明回購資金來源。短期國庫券向來是調節融資需求的主要工具；Wells Fargo估計，若每季回購維持$320億，至11月5日可能需要額外發行約$120億國庫券，之後每季增加約$160億。相較每月約$2.25兆的國庫券總標售額，增量有限，但本質上仍是以更頻繁到期、需要續借的債務，替換部分長期借款。

政府的整體融資需求則持續擴張。截至週二收盤，公共債務達$40.05兆，比2022年1月增加約三分之一。本會計年度累計利息支出為$1.17兆，年增15%，已是僅次於醫療與社會安全保障的第3大預算支出。會計年度前10個月赤字達$1.8兆，較去年同期擴大5%，法定債務上限為$41.1兆。回購可以調整到期結構，不能消除資金缺口。

臨時改動剛公布的時程也有代價。發債安排可預測，有助降低融資不確定性；若意外調整反覆出現，尤其市場認為11月選舉前的政治考量介入債務管理，未來指引的可信度可能受損。回購較舊、流動性較差的非指標券仍有其功能，財政部通常也能收到大量品質良好的賣出報價。措施能否長期影響殖利率，取決於執行是否一致，以及如何與整體借款計畫配合。

## Fed會議紀錄顯示，鷹派陣營不只3張反對票

Fed七月以9比3維持利率於3.5%至3.75%，Logan、Hammack與Kashkari主張升息25個基點，這也是連續第5次維持利率不變。數名與會者支持緊縮，許多官員表示，若通膨未下降，就有必要升息。今年沒有投票權的Schmid與Musalem也曾表明，若能投票，會支持升息。

多數官員預期，關稅及先前能源漲價的影響消退後，通膨將逐步降低；但19名決策官員中，近半數仍擔心通膨比預期頑強，伊朗戰事又增加了不確定性。會後公布的資料卻偏弱：七月就業人數減少、前幾個月新增就業下修、核心通膨溫和，零售銷售更出現1年多來最大降幅。會議紀錄公布前，期貨反映的九月升息機率約36%，已低於七月底逾70%的水準。

2年期殖利率當日持平，與這段資訊落差相呼應：紀錄呈現的是一場偏鷹的討論，卻發生在最新疲弱數據之前。當時官員認為勞動市場穩定且均衡，資本投資與生產力仍強。如今對利率敏感的活動轉弱，投資卻保持韌性，經濟並非全面朝同一方向減速。

住宅市場尤其吃力。30年期房貸平均利率仍達6.67%，伊朗衝突前則低於6%。七月成屋待完成交易量追平2001年有資料以來的次低水準，Redfin估計賣方人數比買方多51.3%。房價仍接近六月$43.4萬的中位數紀錄，獨棟住宅開工卻降至2022年以來最低。若美債漲勢持續，融資成本可望下降，但房市已同時面臨負擔能力不足與成交低迷。

主席Warsh提議將每年定期政策會議從8次減至6次，今年不會實施。會議減少，可讓官員在兩次決策間取得更多資料，也會使市場風險集中在較少的日期。眼前更重要的是他即將在Jackson Hole的談話，尤其如何衡量會後出現的經濟放緩，與七月紀錄中的通膨疑慮。

能源風險仍在。阿聯稱遭飛彈攻擊後，停止與伊朗的貿易及金融交易，帶動布蘭特原油上漲0.60%至$91.57，近1週漲幅達2.91%。伊朗否認責任，航班仍持續運行。另一方面，Saudi Aramco向至少3家歐洲煉油廠保證九月足額供油。WTI下跌0.67%至$84.37，兩種油價走勢分歧，並未形成一致的通膨降溫訊號。

實質美債殖利率下降之際，美元指數下跌0.82%至98.831，黃金期貨上漲4.69%至$4,570.90。股市反應較不一致：S&P 500上漲0.21%，VIX下跌6.00%至14.89，Nasdaq 100卻下跌0.22%，半導體指數跌2.12%，近1週跌幅擴大至5.33%。利率回落支撐大盤，仍未止住科技股賣壓。

## Alphabet募資成功，AI融資延伸至可轉債與夾層債

Alphabet首次發行澳幣債，吸引逾A$180億訂單，最終規模由原先約A$50億提高至A$55億。其中A$10億的20年期債殖利率為6.98%，較當地基準高180個基點，創Alphabet歷來發債殖利率新高。金額最大的A$15億浮動利率券，同時也是需求最強的一檔。

這筆已完成交易，讓市場看到Alphabet進入新幣別市場的實際成本。公司持有S&P次高評等，今年資本支出預估最高$2,050億，除澳幣外，也曾透過美元、瑞郎、英鎊、歐元、加幣與日圓籌資。強健的資產負債表有助開拓市場，卻無法隔絕各地公債殖利率偏高的影響；對投資人而言，Alphabet債券也成為政府債以外的高品質選擇。

Nebius則推出$45億可轉債，分為2030年到期的$27.5億、擬議票息0%至0.5%，以及2034年到期的$17.5億、擬議票息4%至4.5%。這家總部位於阿姆斯特丹的AI雲端業者，今年稍早已發行約$43億可轉債。股價截至週二累漲197%，消息後在美股盤前一度下跌9.2%。交易預計週三稍晚定價，上述票息仍是行銷條件，尚非最終結果。轉換權降低了現金利息負擔，代價是未來股權可能遭到稀釋。

Nexus Data Centers位於德州Hubbard、占地2,900英畝的園區，則在$160億融資中，取得Eagle Point Credit Management約$13億夾層債資金。Anthropic是主要租戶，園區包含燃氣發電廠，Google同意保證優先債務；Eagle Point的受償順位低於這一受保證層級。整筆融資最初僅約$1.5億，以土地擔保的優先債起步，隨租戶及保證安排逐步成形而多次擴大。

相較融資總額，各層債權的差別更值得注意。園區與電廠仍須完成興建並投入營運，優先債保證也不涵蓋夾層債。Nexus可能在今年稍晚發行高收益債，為銀行主導的$150億部分進行再融資。施工貸款銀行與日後債券投資人將在不同階段承擔風險，回收金額仍取決於擔保品、保證範圍與再融資條件。

另一筆規劃中的交易將考驗較弱租戶的信用。Digital Drive擬於九月發行$11.5億債券，標的是維吉尼亞州、出租給投機級CoreWeave的資料中心。作為比較，Galaxy Digital七月一筆$35億、同樣與CoreWeave相關的融資，付出10%的成本。美債殖利率下降可降低基準利率，租戶與專案風險仍須另外定價。

整體新債市場依然繁忙。美國八月投資級發行量達$1,520億，連續第3個月創下該月份紀錄；歐洲本週至少發行€385億，為歷來最繁忙的暑假後重啟週。歐洲投資級利差截至週二為77個基點，低於六月底。基金持續流入，支撐芬蘭、Sika、Mizuho等發行人籌資，未被近期政府債賣壓打斷。

長天期公司債也受惠於週三漲勢。美國20年以上AAA至A級指數報酬為1.61%，同天期BBB級為1.51%，已開發市場10年以上美元投資級指數為1.35%。LQD上漲0.69%，HYG與JNK各約上漲0.23%。長久期資產漲幅仍最突出，新債發行則維持活躍。

## 印尼按兵不動，通膨變化使新興市場曲線分歧

印尼央行在今年累計升息100個基點後，連續第2個月維持政策利率於5.75%。代理總裁Destry Damayanti重申匯率穩定優先，並將自九月第2週擴大避險獎勵計畫。央行將持續在境內、境外干預匯市，同時運用總體審慎措施支持放款。印尼盾收升0.1%，10年期公債殖利率下跌5個基點至7.11%，為近2個月最低。

央行沒有以提高SRBI收益率吸引外幣資金，而是搭配獎勵措施、縮減發行。12個月期SRBI平均收益率已在8月14日下降22個基點。七月國內信用年增13.58%，為至少疫情以來最快，進一步回收流動性的吸引力因而降低。這套安排保留匯率防線，同時支援國內放款。

南非通膨降幅超過預期。七月整體年增率由5.0%降至4.3%，低於4.5%的市場預期，月增率也由0.7%降至0.2%。商品通膨從4.8%降至3.4%，服務從5.2%降至5.0%，食品降至0.6%，為2010年以來最低。不過，核心通膨由4.1%小幅升至4.2%。10年期殖利率下跌2個基點至8.68%，遠期利率協議仍反映9月23日升息25個基點的機率為70%。

印度8月3日至5日會議紀錄顯示，6名委員一致維持附買回利率於5.25%，並連續第4次維持中性立場。總裁Sanjay Malhotra警告，食品、燃料與其他投入成本的壓力可能擴散。副總裁Poonam Gupta表示，今年稍晚可能需要升息，10至12月通膨預估將達5.9%。央行將本會計年度成長預測上修至6.7%，通膨預測下修至5%，暫時保留觀察能源衝擊的時間。

南韓市場對近期大幅緊縮的疑慮減輕，支撐了短債，卻未保護長端。3年期殖利率較七月底高點下降13個基點，10年期自二月底以來則上升約90個基點，使3年與10年期利差擴至近54個基點，為2021年10月以來最寬。LS Securities預期，七月升息25個基點後，今年僅再升息一次，2027年上半年終點利率為3.25%。石油依賴與全球長債賣壓，仍持續影響較長天期。

## 主權債修復與私募信貸損失，各有不同的資產負債表

埃及美元主權債利差上週底降至322個基點，為2014年以來最低，較三月收窄約150個基點。外匯存底創$563億紀錄，匯率更具彈性，加上匯款、旅遊、蘇伊士運河收入及IMF審查後撥付的$18億，改善了對外融資條件。不過，總融資需求偏高與民營化進展緩慢仍是弱點；經過這波行情，投資人能取得的利差補償已減少。

烏克蘭2029年到期債交易價格接近面額85%，殖利率13%，2025年6月價格則為58%。歐洲核准€900億貸款、軍事調整與債權重整，使市場認為資金支應時間有所延長。今年主權債已上漲12%，但債務預估將在2027年達GDP的110%，攻擊行動也可能使穀物出口減半。價格能否繼續修復，仍高度取決於外援與戰局。

私募信貸方面，據知情人士透露，現屬BlackRock的HPS與Oaktree取得MBS Group控制權，將最多$9億債務轉為股權，並再投入$4,000萬。HPS原持有$6億第一順位擔保債，Oaktree持有$3億次順位擔保債。借款成本上升、影視製作減弱及2023年勞工罷工損害了片廠服務業務，原股東Hackman Capital Partners與Affinius Capital因此失去控制權。貸款人轉為股東後，持股價值將仰賴企業營運復甦。

## 先看日本長債標售，九月再看美國回購實際規模

日本8月20日標售20年期公債，是美債反彈後最近的長債需求考驗。標售前殖利率約3.775%，仍接近七月3.89%的高點。市場反映九月日本央行升息機率約四分之三，國內機構對超長債仍審慎。投標倍數、尾差與標售後交易，可看出這樣的殖利率能否在日本本身的政策及財政壓力下，吸引較持久的買盤。

美國方面，Warsh的Jackson Hole談話，以及接下來的就業、零售與通膨資料，將更新Fed在近期疲弱數據公布前形成的討論。這對短端尤其重要：財政部可以改變長債供給，Fed利率預期仍取決於通膨與經濟活動。

擴大回購將於9月9日啟動。各次操作金額、配套國庫券融資及長天期附息債標售指引是否調整，將讓投資人更具體掌握供給變化。週三市場已先大幅反應；政府仍須籌措龐大赤字資金，要延續漲勢，官方買盤之外也需要民間需求接力。

overall_summary.headline: 財政部加碼回購，長債殖利率大幅回落
overall_summary.session_narrative:
財政部將自9月9日起，把支持流動性的10至30年期公債回購規模至少加倍。10年期殖利率下跌6個基點至4.65%，降幅全數來自實質殖利率；2年期持平於4.19%。交易放量，曲線趨平。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Treasury steps in as long borrowing costs climb

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent gave long-bond buyers a reason to return on Wednesday: the department will at least double its liquidity-support purchases of securities maturing in 10 to 30 years. The surprise change, just two weeks after Treasury left the program unchanged in its quarterly financing announcement, sent the 30-year yield down 9 basis points to 5.19%. Ten-year yields fell 6 basis points to 4.65%, while the 2-year held at 4.19%.

The rally came entirely through real yields at the 10-year maturity. Inflation compensation stayed at 2.30%, leaving little evidence that investors had revised down the inflation outlook. Instead, Treasury offered to absorb more long-dated debt after yields had risen above 5.30%. The dollar fell to a three-month low and gold jumped, even as July Fed minutes showed substantial support for higher policy rates. Debt management had eased pressure at the long end without settling the central bank's inflation concerns.

Borrowers continued to raise large sums against that backdrop. Alphabet completed a larger-than-planned Australian-dollar debut, paying 6.98% on its longest tranche despite strong demand. Nebius turned again to convertible debt, and an Anthropic-linked Texas development drew mezzanine financing beneath a Google-guaranteed senior layer. The deals extended the AI funding cycle across currencies and capital structures. Lower Treasury yields help the borrowing cost, but the terms still depend heavily on who guarantees repayment and who bears construction or equity risk.

## A larger buyback changes the supply mix, not the deficit

The expanded operations begin September 9. Treasury's previous tentative calendar, running through November 4, allowed up to $14 billion of purchases in the 10- to 30-year sector. Doubling that amount implies at least another $14 billion; Barclays estimated about $16 billion of extra purchases per quarter, equivalent to roughly 15% of annual 20- and 30-year supply. Those sums are modest relative to the Treasury market, but large enough to affect the amount of long duration available to private investors.

Timing amplified the announcement. Treasury normally sets buyback parameters at quarterly refundings and had reaffirmed the existing schedule only two weeks earlier. The mid-quarter revision suggested that higher long borrowing costs had become uncomfortable for officials, even though trading remained orderly. Investors now have to consider both the planned supply of bonds and the possibility of further changes if yields rise again.

Wednesday's move drew heavy trading. Treasury turnover reached $1.370 trillion in original-face par value, up 28.1% from the previous session; nominal coupons accounted for $1.112 trillion, up 31.5%. Trading in the 7- to 10-year bucket rose 53.1% to $234.3 billion, while maturities beyond 20 years rose 52.0% to $170.7 billion. Dealer-to-customer transactions made up 39.9% and 46.0% of those buckets. These are turnover figures rather than net flows, but they show that the rally occurred amid substantial activity. The 20-plus-year government bond index gained 1.69%, against 0.03% for the 1- to 3-year index.

Five-year yields closed 2 basis points lower at 4.35%. The larger long-end gains narrowed 2s10s by 6 basis points to 46 and 2s30s by 9 to 100. Ten-year real yields fell to 2.35%; at 30 years, the 9-basis-point nominal decline also matched the fall in real yields. Even after the rally, 10- and 30-year nominal yields remained 10 and 13 basis points above their levels a month earlier, with 10-year breakevens up 6.

Treasury did not specify how it would finance the purchases. Bills are its usual balancing instrument, and Wells Fargo estimated that a sustained $32 billion quarterly buyback pace could require about $12 billion of additional bill issuance through November 5 and $16 billion per quarter thereafter. That is small beside gross monthly bill auctions near $2.25 trillion. It nevertheless exchanges some long-term borrowing for debt that must be refinanced more often.

The underlying financing need continues to grow. Public debt reached $40.05 trillion at Tuesday's close, a third higher than in January 2022. Fiscal-year-to-date interest expense was $1.17 trillion, up 15% and already the third-largest budget category after healthcare and Social Security. The deficit through the fiscal year's first ten months reached $1.8 trillion, 5% wider than a year earlier, against a debt ceiling of $41.1 trillion. Buybacks can alter the maturity mix; they do not eliminate that shortfall.

There is also a trade-off in changing a schedule investors had just received. Predictable issuance helps reduce financing uncertainty. Repeated surprise revisions could make future guidance less dependable, particularly if investors see political objectives ahead of November's elections influencing debt management. The program still serves a liquidity purpose in older, off-the-run securities, for which Treasury routinely receives large volumes of high-quality offers. Its longer-term influence on yields will depend on how consistently it is run alongside the government's wider borrowing program.

## Fed minutes reveal a wider hawkish bloc

The July meeting produced a 9-3 vote to keep rates at 3.5%–3.75%, with Lorie Logan, Beth Hammack and Neel Kashkari preferring a 25-basis-point increase. The decision extended a run of five consecutive holds. Several participants favored tightening, and many said an increase would be necessary if inflation did not decline. Nonvoters Jeff Schmid and Alberto Musalem have also said they would have supported a hike.

Most officials expected inflation to ease as tariff effects and earlier energy increases faded, but nearly half of the 19 policymakers saw a risk of greater persistence. The Iran war added uncertainty. Since that meeting, however, employers have cut jobs in July, earlier hiring has been revised lower, core inflation has been subdued and retail sales have recorded their largest decline in more than a year. Before the minutes, futures implied about a 36% chance of a September hike, down from more than 70% at the end of July.

That sequence helps explain the unchanged 2-year yield: the minutes documented a hawkish discussion, but one held before the latest weak data. Officials had described the labor market as stable and balanced, with strong capital investment and productivity. They now face softer interest-sensitive activity alongside continuing investment strength rather than a uniform slowdown.

Housing illustrates the strain. The average 30-year mortgage rate remained 6.67%, compared with less than 6% before the Iran conflict. July pending existing-home sales matched the second-weakest reading since records began in 2001; Redfin counted 51.3% more sellers than buyers. Prices were still near June's record median of $434,000, while single-family starts were the weakest since 2022. A sustained Treasury rally would help financing costs, but it would reach a housing market already struggling with affordability and low turnover.

Chair Kevin Warsh's proposal to reduce scheduled policy meetings from eight to six would not take effect this year. Fewer meetings could give officials more data between decisions, while concentrating market attention on a smaller number of dates. His forthcoming Jackson Hole remarks will be more immediately relevant: investors will look for how he weighs the post-meeting slowdown against the inflation concerns recorded in July.

Energy has not removed those concerns. Brent rose 0.60% to $91.57, up 2.91% over a week, after the UAE halted trade and financial transactions with Iran following an alleged missile attack. Iran denied responsibility, and flights continued. Saudi Aramco separately assured at least three European refiners of full September crude volumes. WTI fell 0.67% to $84.37, leaving a mixed oil close rather than a common disinflation signal.

The dollar index dropped 0.82% to 98.831 and gold futures gained 4.69% to $4,570.90 as real Treasury yields fell. Equities were less uniform: the S&P 500 rose 0.21% and VIX fell 6.00% to 14.89, but Nasdaq 100 lost 0.22% and semiconductors fell 2.12%, taking their weekly decline to 5.33%. Broad markets welcomed the rates relief without ending the selloff in technology.

## Alphabet finds demand; AI financing reaches deeper into the capital structure

Alphabet sold A$5.5 billion in its Australian-dollar debut, above the roughly A$5 billion initially contemplated, after attracting more than A$18 billion of orders. Its A$1 billion 20-year tranche yielded 6.98%, or 180 basis points over the local benchmark—the highest note yield Alphabet has paid. The largest tranche, a A$1.5 billion floating-rate note, also received the most demand.

The completed transaction puts a price on the company's expansion into another funding market. Alphabet holds S&P's second-highest rating and expects capital spending of as much as $205 billion this year. It has tapped US dollars, Swiss francs, sterling, euros, Canadian dollars and yen as well as Australian dollars. A strong balance sheet opens those markets, but it does not insulate the company from elevated underlying government yields. Its bonds also give investors another high-quality alternative to sovereign debt.

Nebius launched $4.5 billion of convertibles in two series: $2.75 billion due in 2030 with a proposed 0%–0.5% coupon and $1.75 billion due in 2034 at 4%–4.5%. The Amsterdam-based AI cloud provider had already issued about $4.3 billion of convertibles earlier this year. Its shares fell as much as 9.2% before the US open after gaining 197% through Tuesday. Pricing was expected later Wednesday; the coupons remained marketing terms, not final results. The conversion option reduces the cash interest burden in exchange for potential equity dilution.

At Nexus Data Centers' 2,900-acre campus in Hubbard, Texas, Eagle Point Credit Management supplied roughly $1.3 billion of mezzanine debt within a $16 billion financing. Anthropic is the primary tenant, the project includes a gas-fired power plant, and Google agreed to guarantee senior debt. Eagle Point's claim ranks below that protected layer. The financing began with about $150 million of senior secured debt backed by land and grew repeatedly as the tenant and guarantee arrangements developed.

The distinction between those layers matters more than the headline financing size. The campus and power plant still have to be built and operated, and the senior guarantee does not extend to the mezzanine tranche. Nexus may seek high-yield bonds later this year to refinance the $15 billion bank-led portion. Construction lenders and eventual bondholders would therefore enter at different stages, with recovery depending on collateral, guarantee scope and the terms of refinancing.

Another planned sale will test a weaker tenant credit. Digital Drive proposes $1.15 billion of bonds in September for a Virginia data center leased to speculative-grade CoreWeave. As a comparison, Galaxy Digital paid 10% on a $3.5 billion CoreWeave-linked deal in July. Treasury relief may lower the benchmark rate, but investors will still have to price the tenant and project risks separately.

The wider issuance market stayed busy. US investment-grade sales reached $152 billion for August, a third consecutive monthly record, while European borrowers issued at least €38.5 billion this week in the busiest post-summer restart on record. European IG spreads stood at 77 basis points at Tuesday's close, below end-June levels. Strong fund inflows supported deals from Finland, Sika, Mizuho and others despite the recent sovereign selloff.

Long corporate bonds benefited from Wednesday's rally: the US 20-plus-year AAA–A index returned 1.61%, the comparable BBB index 1.51%, and a developed-market 10-plus-year dollar IG index 1.35%. LQD gained 0.69%, while HYG and JNK each rose about 0.23%. The strongest gains remained in long duration, alongside an active primary market.

## Indonesia holds; inflation surprises divide emerging-market curves

Bank Indonesia kept its policy rate at 5.75% for a second month after 100 basis points of increases this year. Acting Governor Destry Damayanti reaffirmed currency stability as the priority, while expanding a hedging incentive program from the second week of September. The bank will continue onshore and offshore intervention and use macroprudential measures to support lending. The rupiah closed 0.1% stronger and the 10-year government yield fell 5 basis points to 7.11%, its lowest in almost two months.

Rather than raise SRBI yields to attract foreign currency, the bank is using incentives while reducing issuance. The average 12-month SRBI yield fell 22 basis points on August 14. Domestic credit growth reached 13.58% in July, the fastest since at least the pandemic, making further liquidity withdrawal less attractive. The policy preserves support for lending while leaving currency defense in place.

South African inflation slowed more than expected. July's annual headline rate fell to 4.3% from 5.0%, below the 4.5% consensus, and the monthly increase eased to 0.2% from 0.7%. Goods inflation declined to 3.4% from 4.8%, services to 5.0% from 5.2%, and food to 0.6%, the lowest since 2010. Core inflation nevertheless edged up to 4.2% from 4.1%. Ten-year yields fell 2 basis points to 8.68%, but forward-rate agreements still priced a 70% probability of a 25-basis-point increase on September 23.

India's August 3–5 minutes showed a unanimous six-member decision to hold the repo rate at 5.25% and retain a neutral stance for a fourth meeting. Governor Sanjay Malhotra warned that food, fuel and other input-cost pressures could broaden. Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta said a hike might become necessary later in the year, with inflation projected at 5.9% in October–December. The RBI raised its fiscal-year growth forecast to 6.7% and cut its inflation forecast to 5%, allowing time to assess the energy shock.

In Korea, doubts about aggressive near-term tightening have helped shorter bonds without protecting the long end. The 3-year yield has fallen 13 basis points from its late-July peak, while the 10-year has risen about 90 basis points since end-February. The 3s10s spread reached almost 54 basis points, its widest since October 2021. LS Securities expects only one further hike this year after July's 25-basis-point increase, and a 3.25% terminal rate in the first half of 2027. Oil dependence and the global long-bond selloff continue to weigh further along the curve.

## Sovereign recoveries and a private-credit loss depend on different balance sheets

Egypt's sovereign dollar spread ended the prior week at 322 basis points, the lowest since 2014 and about 150 basis points tighter since March. Record reserves of $56.3 billion, a more flexible pound, remittances, tourism and Suez Canal receipts have improved external funding, alongside $1.8 billion released after an IMF review. High gross financing needs and slow privatization remain weaknesses. After the rally, investors receive less spread compensation for those risks.

Ukraine's 2029 notes traded near 85 cents and yielded 13%, compared with a price of 58 cents in June 2025. European approval of a €90 billion loan, military adaptation and creditor restructurings have extended the perceived financing runway. Sovereign bonds have returned 12% this year, although debt is projected to reach 110% of GDP by 2027 and attacks threaten to halve grain exports. Further recovery rests heavily on aid and the course of the war.

In private credit, HPS, now owned by BlackRock, and Oaktree took control of MBS Group by converting as much as $900 million of debt into equity and committing another $40 million, according to people familiar with the transaction. HPS held a $600 million first lien and Oaktree a $300 million junior lien. Higher borrowing costs, weaker film production and the 2023 labor strikes had impaired the studio-services business, displacing owners Hackman Capital Partners and Affinius Capital. The lenders now hold ownership stakes whose value depends on an operating recovery.

## Japan's auction comes first; Treasury's larger purchases start in September

Japan's August 20 sale of 20-year debt is the nearest test of long-bond demand after the US rally. The yield entered the auction near 3.775%, still close to July's 3.89% peak. Markets assigned roughly a three-quarters probability to a September BOJ increase, and domestic institutions remained cautious about superlong debt. The bid-to-cover ratio, tail and subsequent trading will show whether those yields attract durable buyers despite Japan's own policy and fiscal pressures.

In the US, Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks and the next employment, retail and inflation releases will update a Fed debate recorded before the recent weak data. The distinction is important for the front end: Treasury can change the supply of long bonds, but Fed pricing still depends on inflation and activity.

The larger buybacks begin September 9. Operation sizes, associated bill financing and any revisions to long-coupon auction guidance will give investors a firmer measure of the supply adjustment. Wednesday delivered a sizeable first response; sustaining it will require private demand alongside official purchases while the government continues to finance a large deficit.
